findings.title: Index used as key on a list whose rows hold uncontrolled input state
findings.explanation: The list is built with map((t, i) => ...) and keyed by index (line 7). Each row holds an uncontrolled <input defaultValue={t.text}> whose DOM value is per-instance state. When onRemove deletes a row above a row the user has already edited, React reuses the instance at the old index: defaultValue changes do not overwrite a dirty input, so the edited text stays on the wrong todo. Example: rows [A, B, C], user edits row 2 (B) to 'B edited', then removes A. Row 1 now shows B's text as its default value but the DOM still shows 'A'; row 2 shows 'B edited' against todo C. The list is reorderable by removal, so the index key is not stable. Other occurrences: none. Assumption: rows are removed through onRemove by the parent, as the props indicate.
findings.suggested_fix: Key the rows by the stable id: change the map to (t) => <li key={t.id}> (or keep the index-free signature and use t.id), and keep the input keyed to that id so React preserves each row's state when rows are removed.

findings.title: Full 50k-row sort and filter run on every keystroke render
findings.explanation: The comment at line 5 states players holds about 50,000 rows loaded in one request, which is the evidenced size. The component re-renders on every keystroke because setQuery is called from the input's onChange (line 14). Each render copies and sorts all 50,000 rows (line 8) and then filters them (line 9) before slicing to 20 visible rows. The sort does not depend on query, so the work is repeated on every keypress for unchanged data, blocking the main thread and making typing janky. Other occurrences: the filter on line 9 is part of the same root cause.
findings.suggested_fix: Compute the sorted array once per players change: const ranked = useMemo(() => [...players].sort((a, b) => b.score - a.score), [players]); then filter and slice the memoized array per query. Alternatively sort once upstream or paginate/virtualize the results.

limitations: Reviewed only the files in fixtures/rendering: package.json, tsconfig.json, src/Leaderboard.tsx and src/TodoList.tsx. No next.config, ESLint config or lockfile is present, so Next.js and lint-suppression checks could not be performed.

Rendering-category references were applied in depth. Hooks, TypeScript, Next.js and accessibility checks were made against the same code without a finding, but their references were not loaded in full.
The 50,000-row size in Leaderboard.tsx comes from a code comment, not a runtime measurement. Render cost was not profiled.
The TodoList finding assumes the parent removes rows via onRemove and that React's dirty-value behaviour for uncontrolled inputs applies, as in current React 18. Behaviour was not run.
